title: Cluster’s deceptive serenity hides violent past
caption: The globular cluster Messier 12, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Messier 12 · constellation Ophiuchus · about 23000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Stars crowd into this Hubble image of Messier 12, a globular cluster whose high concentration of stars makes it a fine photographic subject. Its distance is about 23 000 light-years, in the direction of Ophiuchus, the Serpent Bearer. The calm appearance is deceptive, because this cluster seems to have had a violent past.

Crowded quarters in globular clusters can create exotic binary systems, in which two stars are locked in tight orbits and one devours matter from the other, giving off X-rays. Such X-ray binaries are thought to form in very close stellar encounters, and even though Messier 12 is fairly spread out for a globular cluster, X-ray sources have been found in it.

Messier 12 also has far fewer low-mass stars than expected. Using ESO's Very Large Telescope, astronomers gauged how bright and what color more than 16 000 of its 200 000 stars are. Their speculation is that close to one million low-mass stars were pulled away as the cluster passed through the densest parts of the Milky Way on its orbit around the galactic center.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.26 x 3.10 arcminutes) and distance (23000 light years), the frame spans roughly 22 × 21 light-years. Its light set out about 23,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. A blue filter (F435W) is shown in blue, a red filter (F625W) in green and a near-infrared filter (F814W) in red.
understand.eye: The near-infrared exposure records light the eye cannot see, and the red filter is displayed as green, so the colors are not exactly those the eye would perceive.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image was taken with the Advanced Camera for Surveys' Wide Field Channel. Exposure times were 1360 seconds through the blue filter, 200 seconds through the red filter and 364 seconds in the near-infrared, and the frame spans about 3.2 by 3.1 arcminutes.
alt: A crowded globular cluster of stars.
